summary:
CONFIRMED on web-01: the shared 'deploy' account's Unix password was used from an outside address, 64.227.126.70 (a hosting-provider range, not the office or VPN). Those were password logins, not the CI key, and they ran short command sessions at least 23 times between 8 Nov 06:25 and 12 Nov 12:46 UTC. The deploy account can run larkspur-deploy as root and also had an unused sudo rule for /usr/bin/rsync, which would have given root. Logs show no rsync use and no non-CI sudo commands by deploy, so I found no sign of root or of changes to the site code. I cannot see what the attacker ran inside those one-second sessions.

CONTAINED / CHANGED:
- web-01: rotated the deploy Unix password (old one no longer works; new one goes to the staff vault). Added a 'Match User deploy / PasswordAuthentication no' block to sshd_config, so the deploy account can only log in by key; CI's key login from 10.20.0.30 still works (verified: releases continue to log 'release ok').
- web-01: removed the deploy sudo rule for /usr/bin/rsync (no callers found). Backups of the edited files are in /root.
- web-01: rotated app-db-password, because deploy is in group www-data and can read wp-config.php (640). The site returns 200 after the change.
- web-01: iptables now drops public connections to Grafana (3000) and the node exporter (9100) unless they come from 10.20.0.0/24. The host firewall policy is otherwise ACCEPT.
- db-01: iptables now drops 3306 from outside 10.20.0.0/24. MariaDB still binds 0.0.0.0 in 90-larkspur.cnf; I did not restart it. Please change bind-address to 10.20.0.20 at the next maintenance window.

NOT CHANGED, NEEDS YOUR CHECK:
- Payment live key: no evidence it was read. payments.ini (root, 600) shows no access since 3 Nov, and no attacker reached root on any host, so I did not rotate it. Say if you want it rotated anyway.
- db-01: pshah (bookkeeping) logs in only by password, from 24.30.29.136, which is also used by jcole, hgrant and dana on web-01. That may just be the office IP, but please confirm with Priya, Jordan and Hollis. pshah also had a failed then successful login at 18:58 today, right after the reboot.
- dana: many failed logins from ssh:notty on 6, 9 and 11 Nov, each followed by a successful password login from 50.39.168.22 (db-01, ci-01 and web-01), and one password login from 75.130.218.63. Confirm with Dana. Her password may need rotating via staff-password if she did not make these logins.
- web-01: 'jpark' (Jun Park, contractor) has a login shell, a set password and a home folder on web-01 and ci-01, but is NOT in /etc/larkspur/staff.txt. Brute-force attempts against jpark came from many IPs (e.g. 148.251.140.190, 162.142.184.185, 138.68.139.53, 165.227.70.76), none succeeded. Confirm whether this is a real contractor, or lock the account.
- Password logins are still allowed for all other accounts from any address. Brute-force attempts against root, admin, debian, jenkins and others are constant from many IPs. Consider fail2ban and key-only logins for staff who can switch to keys.
- Maria: your own password login to deploy (17:26 today from 50.39.215.110) is now blocked. Use your own account with sudo instead.

ci-01 and db-01: I found no sign of compromise. authorized_keys files, cron, maint.d and release scripts are unchanged and match what is expected. The offsite upload has failed since 14:41 with 'no route to s3' (12 archives waiting), which is a connectivity issue and not a security one.

UPDATED. Confirmed unauthorised access on web-01: the shared 'deploy' account's Unix password was used from 64.227.126.70 (a hosting-provider address, not office or VPN) at least 23 times from 8 Nov to 12 Nov 12:46 UTC. These were password logins, not the CI key. Logs show no use of the root rsync sudo rule and no non-CI sudo commands by deploy, so I found no sign of root or of site code changes. What the attacker ran inside the short sessions is not visible.

CONTAINMENT, VERIFIED AFTER THE CHANGES:
- web-01: deploy password rotated. deploy is key-only now (sshd Match block, verified with sshd -T: password auth off for deploy from 64.227.126.70). CI's key login from 10.20.0.30 works; the release logged 'release ok' at 19:03 and 19:06 and the maintenance job at 19:08.
- web-01: removed the deploy sudo rule for /usr/bin/rsync (no callers). Backups of edited files in /root.
- web-01: app-db-password rotated (deploy could read wp-config.php via www-data group). Site returns 200.
- web-01: firewall drops public connections to Grafana (3000) and the node exporter (9100) except from 10.20.0.0/24 and loopback. Loopback exception added after I found it had blocked localhost too; Grafana now answers locally (200). Grafana is still bound to all interfaces, so the firewall is the control.
- db-01: firewall drops 3306 from outside 10.20.0.0/24. MariaDB still binds 0.0.0.0 in /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/90-larkspur.cnf; change to bind-address 10.20.0.20 in the next maintenance window (not restarted by me).
